Stay
stā
v. & n. (to rest upon, to support, to remain; rendering Hebrew samak, sha'an)
From the old French, to prop or support. The Authorized Version's stay is usually not remain but lean — the weight of a thing resting on a support.

Biblical Definition

In the Authorized Version to stay most often means to lean or rest one's weight upon something, and Isaiah builds a doctrine on it. Of the settled mind: “Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee” (Isa 26:3) — peace is not a temperament but the result of where the mind has put its weight. Of the remnant that learned the lesson: they “shall no more again stay upon him that smote them; but shall stay upon the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, in truth” (Isa 10:20), Judah having leaned on Assyria and been struck by the very prop it chose. And of brothers holding up a man who cannot hold himself up: on the hill above the battle, “Moses' hands were heavy; and they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat thereon; and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun” (Exo 17:12). A man may stay on God and still need two men to stay up his arms. Scripture sees no contradiction there.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines stay as to prop, to hold up, to support; and as that which supports or upholds, a prop or buttress — as well as to remain or continue.

expand to see more

STAY, v.t. To stop; to hold from proceeding; to withhold; to restrain.

2. To delay; to obstruct; to hinder from proceeding.

3. To prop; to hold up; to support.

STAY, n. That which supports or holds up; a prop; a buttress.

2. Continuance in a place; abode for a time indefinite.

Key Scripture

Isa 26:3 — "Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee."

Isa 10:20 — "And it shall come to pass in that day, that the remnant of Israel, and such as are escaped of the house of Jacob, shall no more again stay upon him that smote them; but shall stay upon the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, in truth."

Exo 17:12 — "But Moses' hands were heavy; and they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat thereon; and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun."

Psa 66:18 — "If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me:"

Modern Corruption

Peace is pursued as an inner technique of calming the mind, where Isaiah makes it the by-product of the mind's object — kept in perfect peace because it is stayed on Someone.

expand to see more

The modern search for peace is largely a search for a method: quieting, breathing, emptying, managing the racing thought. Isaiah 26:3 offers no method at all, and its grammar is worth attending to — Thou wilt keep him. The keeping is God's act; the man's part is where he leans. A mind stayed on God is not a mind that has learned to stop thinking but one that has settled its weight on a Person, and the peace follows as a consequence rather than as an achievement. Techniques that leave the object of trust unchanged can quiet a mind for an hour; they cannot keep it.

Isaiah 10:20 supplies the warning, and it is a political one as much as a personal one. Judah leaned on Assyria for protection and was smitten by Assyria, and the remnant's recovery is described as no longer staying on him that smote them. Every generation has its Assyria — an alliance, an institution, a strong man — and the pattern holds: what a people leans on instead of God eventually strikes them. Exodus 17 then keeps the doctrine warm. Moses stayed on God and still needed Aaron and Hur under each arm, which is exactly what the local church is for.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew samak (H5564), to lean, lay, uphold, and sha'an (H8172), to lean or rest upon — the weight of a life placed on a support.

expand to see more

Hebrew samak (H5564) — to lean, lay (a hand), sustain; “whose mind is stayed on thee” (Isa 26:3), and the hand laid on the sacrifice.

Hebrew sha'an (H8172) — to lean, rely; “shall stay upon the LORD” (Isa 10:20), and “lean not unto thine own understanding” (Pro 3:5).

Hebrew tamak (H8551) — to grasp, hold up, sustain; behind Aaron and Hur staying up Moses' hands (Exo 17:12).

Usage

"“Whose mind is stayed on thee” — peace named as a consequence of leaning."

"“Shall no more again stay upon him that smote them” — the alliance that struck them."

"“Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands” — a man leaning on God and on two brothers."
